skill.name: ad-test-designer
skill.description: Use when the user asks to "design an A/B test", "set up a creative/landing test", "run an incrementality test", or "is this result statistically and practically material?"; produces a hypothesis, variant matrix, sample-size/duration/power plan, and a documented effect/uncertainty read from own exported results. It applies only a precommitted owner-approved action rule; the statistical helper never chooses a business action. Not for producing variants — use ad-creative-builder; not for reading back one shipped change — use paid-measurement-loop. 广告AB测试设计/实验设计/显著性判定/增效测试
skill.summary: Design advertising experiments and interpret results with explicit statistical, practical, and decision-ownership rules.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting and relative links to repository documentation. The skill also recommends an unaudited Python helper and can persist test summaries after consent, so those behaviors remain disclosed.

remediation.issue: The recommended experiment.py command executes code that is outside the audited skill files.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle and audit the helper with this skill, pin its integrity, and document its accepted arguments before execution.

remediation.issue: Saved test summaries may contain campaign performance data and decision details.
remediation.suggestion: Describe retention and deletion controls, minimize stored fields, and confirm the destination before every write.

content.value_statement: Advertising tests often produce unclear results because hypotheses, metrics, and decision rules are incomplete. This skill creates structured test plans and interprets exported results with explicit statistical and practical thresholds.
actual_capabilities: Creates falsifiable hypotheses for creative, landing-page, and incrementality tests.
Builds controlled A/B and A/B/n variant matrices that isolate one variable.
Plans sample size, duration, power, alpha, read dates, and guardrail metrics.
Interprets exported conversion results using effect estimates, intervals, and statistical flags.
Separates statistical detection, practical materiality, guardrail status, and owner-approved decisions.
limitations: Requires a baseline, useful lift target, and traffic estimate for complete prospective sizing.
Does not create advertisements, landing-page variants, or campaign assets.
Uses manually exported data unless compatible external connectors are available.
Does not choose a business action without a precommitted rule and named owner.

use_cases.title: Plan a landing-page test
use_cases.description: Define one page change, success metrics, guardrails, sample requirements, and a fixed read date.

use_cases.title: Structure creative testing
use_cases.description: Create a controlled matrix for several ad concepts while preserving attribution and adequate traffic per variant.

use_cases.title: Review completed results
use_cases.description: Separate effect size, uncertainty, practical value, guardrails, and decision authority from an exported experiment summary.

prompt_templates.title: Design a basic A/B test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A/B test for [change]. Baseline conversion is [rate], daily traffic is [volume], and minimum useful lift is [lift].
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with one controlled change and known baseline inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an A/B/n test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an A/B/n matrix for [variants]. Define one changed variable, primary metric, guardrails, sample size, duration, alpha, power, and read date.
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare several creative or landing-page directions.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret completed results
prompt_templates.prompt: Read this exported test summary: [results]. Report rates, lift, interval, statistical status, practical status, guardrails, and any missing decision rule.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate a completed test without turning significance into an automatic action.

prompt_templates.title: Design an incrementality study
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an incrementality test for [campaign]. Specify treatment, holdout, matching, contamination controls, power assumptions, sequential policy, owner, and precommitted action rule.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a controlled study for advanced causal measurement.

output_examples.input: Test a new landing-page hero with a three percent baseline and a fifteen percent minimum useful lift.
output: Hypothesis: the new hero will increase conversion by at least fifteen percent.
Design: equal control and variant allocation with all other page elements fixed.
Plan: declare alpha, power, required exposures, duration, read date, and bounce-rate guardrail.

output_examples.input: Review a completed control and variant conversion test with exported exposure and conversion totals.
output: Read-out: report each rate, absolute difference, relative lift, interval, and declared-alpha status.
Decision: remain undecided when the practical threshold, guardrail rule, or owner approval is missing.

output_examples.input: Plan an incrementality test for a regional prospecting campaign.
output: Structure: match treatment and holdout regions before launch and monitor contamination.
Measurement: precommit the outcome, minimum useful lift, power, test window, and escalation rule.

best_practices: Precommit the hypothesis, primary metric, minimum useful effect, sample size, read date, and decision rule.
Change one variable per variant and keep audience, budget logic, and destination conditions controlled.
Report statistical evidence, practical value, guardrails, provenance, and decision ownership as separate fields.
anti_patterns: Do not stop a fixed-sample test early after observing a favorable result.
Do not compare many variants without adjusting the design for traffic and multiple comparisons.
Do not treat a p-value or helper output as automatic approval to promote or stop a variant.

faq.question: What inputs are needed for a new test?
faq.answer: Provide the proposed change, baseline rate, daily traffic, minimum useful lift, primary metric, and important guardrails.

faq.question: Can it analyze completed test results?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide per-variant exposures and outcomes, plus the declared alpha, practical threshold, and any guardrail rules.

faq.question: Does it generate ad creative?
faq.answer: No. It designs the experiment and interprets results, but another tool must produce the tested assets.

faq.question: Can it choose the winning business action?
faq.answer: Only when a named owner and precommitted action rule already exist. Otherwise, it reports the decision as undecided.

faq.question: Does it require direct platform access?
faq.answer: No. Manual campaign, analytics, or ecommerce exports are sufficient for planning and read-out work.

faq.question: How does it handle early stopping?
faq.answer: It follows the declared sequential policy. Without one, it uses the fixed read date and flags repeated looks as invalid.
